client.name: Kindred Kitchens
client.cause: Ending child food poverty in the UK

exampleLines: No child should start the day on an empty stomach.
A full plate changes a whole week.

proofPoints: Last year Kindred Kitchens provided 310,000 meals across 14 towns
£20 fills a family food parcel for a week
£45 stocks a school breakfast club for a week
£90 funds a week of fresh fruit and veg for a community fridge
9 in 10 families we support have at least one adult in work
Kindred Kitchens has run community kitchens since 2014
complianceNotes: Never photograph children without written parental consent
Gift Aid statement must appear on every donation page
Do not describe families as 'poor' or 'needy'

audience.name: Parents who give
audience.description: UK parents aged 30-50 who already give to children's causes and recognise how fast a tight week becomes an empty cupboard
motivations: Cannot stand the thought of a child going without
Wants to know a gift is used well
objections: Thinks food banks are only for people out of work
Worried the money goes on admin

offer.ask: Help a family eat well this half term

donationTiers.impact: fills a family food parcel for a week
stocks a school breakfast club for a week
funds a week of fresh fruit and veg for a community fridge

offer.matchFunding: Every gift matched by Fairfield Foods until 28 February

keyMessage: When school stops, free school meals stop too. Your gift keeps a family fed through half term, and right now it goes twice as far.

creativeContext.problemInDailyLife: Parents skip meals so their children can eat, and say nothing.
creativeContext.storySeed: My neighbour skipped dinner most nights so her kids could eat, and never told anyone.
creativeContext.openingQuestion: Do you know which family on your street skipped dinner last night?
creativeContext.whatWeDo: runs community kitchens and school breakfast clubs so no child starts the day hungry.
creativeContext.caseStudy: Last February a dad of three in Oldham was working nights and still running out of food by Wednesday. Kindred Kitchens' community fridge and a weekly parcel got the family through half term, and the breakfast club meant the kids ate before school every day. Names and details changed to protect privacy; the case is real.

references: Previous appeal: UGC from a volunteer packing parcels outperformed studio video on ROAS
